tasks.name: state-hook.sh skeleton and event dispatch
tasks.description: Create hooks/state-hook.sh (POSIX sh, executable). It resolves its own directory (following symlinks) to source ../lib/common.sh, reads the full hook JSON from stdin, extracts hook_event_name and session_id with jq, and dispatches to one function per event (stubs for now). Hard rules from the PRD: never `set -e`; trap and swallow all errors; always exit 0; print nothing to stdout or stderr; exit early if jq is missing or session_id is empty. Provide write_state helper that merges a jq object into $state_dir/<session_id>.json (creating it with "v":1 if absent), sets updatedAt=now_ms, sets stateSince=now_ms only when `state` actually changes, and writes atomically.

If none found, omit pid/procStart. Also record cwd and transcript_path from the payload, herdrPane from $HERDR_PANE_ID, termBundleId from $__CFBundleIdentifier, and kind from $CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT (cli→interactive, sdk-* or a -p/--print flag in the parent's args→headless, IDE values→ide, desktop→desktop; unknown→interactive). Write state=idle.

tasks.name: C3 interrupt detection from transcript tail
tasks.description: In the plugin, for sessions busy or waiting after C1/C2 with a readable transcriptPath: read only the last 8192 bytes (tail -c 8192, dropping the first partial line). Find the latest entry that is a real user prompt (type=user with string content or a text block that is not a tool_result). If after it there is a user text entry containing '[Request interrupted by user' (constant INTERRUPT_MARKER) or a type=system entry with subtype=turn_duration, render the session as idle. See tests/fixtures/transcripts/ (denied-permission → idle, completed-turn → idle, esc-before-output → no change). Do not write the state file.

Long-lived children started before stateSince (MCP servers) must not trigger it. Convert lstart to epoch with date -j -f or perl, once per process.

tasks.name: Don't show idle while subagents are still working
tasks.description: When a session's subagents are still running and the parent agent is waiting for them, the row and the menu bar show idle (zzz), although work is going on. Show it as working, or a distinct 'waiting on subagents' state with its own symbol. DISCUSS WITH THE USER BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: which state or symbol to use, whether it counts in the menu bar like busy, and how to detect it reliably (subagents map from SubagentStart/SubagentStop vs Stop ordering, background agents vs foreground ones, stale subagent entries when SubagentStop is missed).

notes.text: When the parent is waiting on running subagents, should it show as working (sparkle, counted as busy) or as a new 'waiting on subagents' state with its own symbol? → Its own 'waiting on subagents' icon.; Should a parent with background subagents still running count as busy in the menu bar, or stay idle since it is ready for your next prompt? → Counted as busy in the menu bar.
New 'subagents' state: hourglass row 'waiting on N subagents', counted as busy in the menu bar; idle parent or parent in Task/Agent tool; interrupt and waiting win; C5 covers missed SubagentStop
